critical_bugs.description: DOC OVERCLAIM (rounding-up): DESIGN.md §3.1.17 and ROADMAP.md M3.3c assert the 768³ result is '31.2 TFLOPS (25.0%) — competitive (≥25% threshold, labeled "competitive" by bench)'. But the bench gates the 'competitive' label on raw `pct >= COMPETITIVE_PCT_THRESHOLD(25.0)`, and 31.2/125*100 = 24.96% < 25.0 — so the bench's OWN code would print the HONEST (non-competitive) label at 31.2 TFLOPS, not 'competitive'. The doc's '25.0%' is a {pct:.1} display-rounding of 24.96; the threshold genuinely requires >=31.25 TFLOPS. Either the true measured value was >=31.25 (then record that, not 31.2) or 'competitive' must be dropped at 768³. As written the doc contradicts the bench's gating arithmetic.

warnings.description: AT-1731/1732 fixture has a row-axis blind spot. A[idx]=(idx%4)+1 with K a multiple of 4 (K=32 and K=48) makes EVERY A row identical (i*K % 4 == 0). Therefore A row-tile 0 (rows 0..15) == A row-tile 1 (rows 16..31) byte-for-byte, and acc_00==acc_10, acc_01==acc_11. A swap of a_mat_0<->a_mat_1, or a swap of the acc_00/acc_10 store offsets (the row axis), would STILL produce max_diff==0 and pass. The docstring/DESIGN claim 'non-symmetric fixture detects A/B index swaps' is only TRUE for the B/column axis (b_mat_0!=b_mat_1, acc_00!=acc_01 verified distinct). The kernel's row indices are correct by code review, but the test provides ZERO mutation-detection power on the A-row / row-store axis. Recommend a fixture where A rows differ (e.g. A[idx]=(idx%7)+1 or include the row index) so a row-tile swap is caught.

summary: Code is correct and the milestone is honestly framed in almost every respect: zero codegen diff, AT-1733 proves 4 distinct well-formed phis, AT-1731/1732 prove RB bit-exact (max_diff==0) end-to-end, kernel A/B reuse indices match the store offsets, FLOP count and GpuTimestamp methodology are sound, the 256³ regression is reported not hidden, and the occupancy tradeoff is stated without overclaiming. ONE blocking honesty defect: at the recorded 768³ = 31.2 TFLOPS the raw pct is 24.96%, which FAILS the bench's own `pct >= 25.0` 'competitive' gate, yet DESIGN.md/ROADMAP.md label it 'competitive (≥25% threshold, labeled by bench)' — a {pct:.1}-rounding overclaim. Fix: either record the genuine >=31.25 measurement or drop the 'competitive' label at 768³. Secondary: the bit-exact fixtures have an A-row blind spot (A rows are degenerate-identical for K multiple of 4), so they cannot catch an a_mat / row-store swap — the 'detects A/B swaps' claim holds only for the column axis. REQUEST_CHANGES on the doc honesty defect; the code itself is mergeable once the label is corrected and the working-tree fixes are committed.
